parsed.headline: Analysts suggest Israel's upcoming election may not alter Iran war policy

pages.text: Regional policymakers and analysts told Arab News that Israel’s election, scheduled for October 20, 2026, may change the country's leader but is unlikely to shift its core strategy regarding Iran. According to these analysts, Iran is expected to remain Israel's chief adversary, military force will continue to be a preferred tool, and Palestinian statehood remains a distant prospect. They suggest the strategic assumptions underpinning Israeli policy were hardened by the October 7, 2023, attacks on southern Israeli communities by Hamas and subsequent wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran. Analysts noted that the real divide between political factions may be one of degree rather than direction, specifically regarding the aggressiveness of warfare, the expansion of Jewish settlements in the West Bank, and the use of diplomacy. Israel’s current security doctrine is described as resting on three pillars: breaking Iran, holding buffer zones beyond its borders, and using force to deter enemies.

The election pits Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud party and its ultranationalist allies against an opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, and his Yashar party. Analysts suggested that a victory for Netanyahu, supported by far-right coalition partners, could potentially embolden him to increase the war with Iran, tighten control over the occupied West Bank, and move diplomacy further to the margins. Aviv Bushinsky, a former adviser to Netanyahu, stated that if Netanyahu is elected, settlement expansion and wars against Iran, Hamas, and Hezbollah will continue, potentially even more aggressively. On October 18, 2026, Netanyahu said Israel must prioritize prevention and offense over containment and defense, including pre-emptive strikes to thwart emerging threats, while maximizing independence in armaments and establishing Israel as a regional power.

parsed.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines loses both legs after vehicle attack in Wangaratta

pages.text: Independent Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both of her legs amputated following an apparent deliberate vehicle attack outside her constituency office in Wangaratta, northeast of Melbourne, her husband confirmed on Wednesday. Haines, 65, was struck by a white Toyota SUV on October 19, 2026. Witnesses reported hearing a bang and seeing a woman pinned between two cars. Following surgery on the night of the incident to treat critical injuries, her left leg was amputated, and doctors proceeded to amputate her right leg on Wednesday after attempting to save it, according to her husband, Phil Haines. Phil Haines stated that while the incident was horrendous, his wife is alive, stable, and in good physical and mental shape. He noted that her recovery will be long and difficult. Counterterrorism investigators have joined a police probe into the incident, though Australian federal police commissioner Krissy Barrett stated there was no intelligence suggesting a prior threat to Haines. Police are still investigating the motive for the attack. 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, a local from nearby Tarrawingee described as an environmental campaigner, appeared in Wangaratta Magistrates' Court on Wednesday. Nugent faces charges of intentionally causing serious injury, dangerous driving causing serious injury, and causing harm to a federal official. Court filings also included charges for the cultivation and possession of cannabis. Police indicated that more charges, including attempted murder, may be laid. During his brief court appearance, Nugent remained silent and emotionless. His lawyer stated that Nugent has a rare neurological condition called idiopathic transverse myelitis and is recovering from a concussion.

parsed.headline: Carney and Ford expected to announce clean auto investment support in Canada

pages.text: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford are expected to unveil a support package for auto companies making clean investments on Parliament Hill this Wednesday afternoon. According to a source with knowledge of the announcement, the package is expected to include measures addressing Canada's greenhouse gas standards following changes made by the Trump administration on October 19, 2026. Carney and Ford are expected to be joined by their respective industry and finance ministers for the rollout.  Industry Minister Mélanie Joly stated on Wednesday that the government intends to provide support to auto companies impacted by the reversal of regulations in the United States. Joly noted that auto producers have been impacted by American tariffs and the decision by the American administration to reduce protections regarding greenhouse gas emissions. She added that the government is working on an electrification strategy that includes subsidies to encourage Canadians to move to electric vehicles.

parsed.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro’s debate gesture sparks viral social media parody in Brazil

pages.text: During a primetime television debate on October 18, 2026, far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro attended the event with the word “corrupto” (corrupt) written on his palm. While intended to highlight the alleged misdeeds of his leftwing opponent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the gesture resulted in a viral social media trend where supporters of Lula parodied the action. Following the debate, individuals across Brazil—including professionals such as nurses, engineers, and teachers, as well as public figures like comedian Antonio Tabet and health minister Alexandre Padilha—posted photographs of their own palms inscribed with their professions or identities. Latin America expert James Bosworth described the stunt as a “critical error” that created a meme image that may persist throughout Bolsonaro's political career. This debate occurred ahead of the presidential runoff, following a first round on October 4 where Bolsonaro received 47.03% of the vote.

parsed.headline: Economists and traders increasingly expect Bank of Canada to raise interest rates

pages.text: A growing number of economists and traders are expecting the Bank of Canada to hike its trend-setting interest rate to address inflation, according to reporting by CBC Canada. While an eighth-consecutive hold was widely predicted for the upcoming week, several institutions have shifted their outlooks. The Bank of Montreal, RBC Dominion Securities, and Desjardins Group have all changed their predictions for October 28 from a hold to a hike. Additionally, Bloomberg data shows that traders in the overnight swap market have increased the odds of a 25-basis point rate hike from 70 per cent to 87 per cent earlier this week as of October 21, 2026. Derek Holt, head of capital markets economics at Scotiabank, is among those calling for a rate hike. The policy rate has remained at 2.25 per cent since a quarter-point cut in October 2025, and the central bank has not raised rates since July 2023.

The shift in expectations follows recent economic data and warnings from Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem. On October 17, 2026, Macklem warned that the bank may need to raise borrowing costs if energy prices remain elevated, noting there is no resolution in sight for the conflict in the Middle East that has impacted global energy markets. On October 19, 2026, Statistics Canada released inflation data highlighting soaring energy costs, though the report noted rising fuel prices had not yet meaningfully spilled into other economic sectors. However, a Bank of Canada survey released the same day found that businesses are bracing for higher prices.

parsed.headline: Thirty Ghanaian journalists receive emerging technology training through UK-led fellowship

pages.text: Thirty journalists in Ghana have completed training in emerging technologies as part of the UK Media Excellence for Emerging Technologies Fellowship. The initiative, led by Imperial Global and the British High Commission in Ghana, is currently in its fourth year and supports the UK-Ghana Science, Technology and Innovation (ST&I) Strategy to deepen cooperation and improve public understanding of scientific developments. The training provided participants with skills in artificial intelligence (AI), climate change, and digital tools, while offering opportunities to engage with researchers and scientists across the country. As part of the programme, fellows visited the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and Environment 360 to observe applications of science, technology, innovation, and the circular economy. Dr. Christian Rogg, the British High Commissioner to Ghana, stated that the fellowship demonstrates how journalism can connect scientific research with public understanding, policy discussions, and potential solutions to societal challenges. At the closing ceremony of the 2026 fellowship, Dr. Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, the Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, called for stronger collaboration between scientists, researchers, and journalists to improve public understanding of science and technology in Ghana. Ten shortlisted journalists and media professionals are expected to participate in an exchange programme at Imperial College London, funded by the British High Commission in Ghana, to gain exposure to international research and scientific communication.

Speaking at a state reception and exchange of greetings held at the Durbar Hall of the Bangabhaban on Wednesday, the President addressed the occasion of Sharadiya Durga Puja and Bijoya Dashami 2026. parsed.headline: Over one million mice and nearly 47,000 rats used annually in Australian research

pages.text: A first-ever nationwide count has found that 1,193,619 mice and 46,961 rats were used for scientific research, teaching, and testing in Australia in 2024. The research, conducted for the Australian and New Zealand Council for the Care of Animals in Research and Teaching, did not include animals bred for research purposes that were not used. The pilot study focused on mice and rats due to their widely defined roles in biomedical research. According to Dr. Malcolm France, a veterinarian who compiled the data, the count is an “overdue first step” toward publishing national statistics for all animals used in research, such as birds, monkeys, fish, and rabbits. Dr. France noted that while the United States, Canada, the European Union, the United Kingdom, and New Zealand use national statistics to inform welfare priorities and transparency, Australia has historically lacked overall data. Establishing the national figure required various approaches, including a freedom of information request. The study found that only New South Wales, Victoria, and Tasmania consistently publish animal use data, while other jurisdictions either collect statistics without sharing them or do neither. Bella Lear, the chief executive of Understanding Animal Research Oceania, stated that nationwide data is “absolutely vital” for Australia to demonstrate its research scope and animal welfare practices.

parsed.headline: Folk Maritime CEO says Saudi Arabia should develop Indian Ocean trade corridor

pages.text: Poul Hestbaek, CEO of Folk Maritime, stated at the Saudi Maritime and Logistics Congress in Jeddah that Saudi Arabia should develop a trade corridor through the Indian Ocean to reduce dependence on the region’s two maritime chokepoints. Speaking on a panel titled “Fragmentation: Navigating the New Geopolitics,” Hestbaek said the Kingdom needs to be independent of the two straits to feel protected in the future, though he noted he did not know how or by whom such a corridor would be developed. According to Hestbaek, Folk Maritime, a company owned by the Public Investment Fund, prioritizes supply security for the Kingdom when making commercial decisions. He described conditions in the Gulf as fragile, noting that while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has returned to approximately 75 percent of normal levels, a single incident could reverse that recovery.
